R2: If someone chases the squirrel then they are blue. ($ChasesSquirrel(x) \implies Blue(x)$)

Since Fact 9 says "The squirrel chases the rabbit", this might be redundant or consistent.
R4: If the squirrel is young then the squirrel is blue. ($Young(Squirrel) \implies Blue(Squirrel)$)
R5: If someone is round then they chase the squirrel. ($Round(x) \implies ChasesSquirrel(x)$)
R6: If someone needs the cat and they are round then they do not chase the rabbit. ($NeedsCat(x) \land Round(x) \implies \neg ChasesRabbit(x)$)

R8: If someone is cold then they like the squirrel. ($Cold(x) \implies LikesSquirrel(x)$)

Derived Fact: The cat is blue.

We just derived that Cat is blue.

Derived Fact: The cat needs the squirrel.
